title: Airbnb Earnings Beat Estimates as Revenue Rises 19% to $4.87 Billion in Q3 Results
excerpt: Airbnb's Q3 diluted EPS of $3.16 topped the $2.85 consensus as revenue beat forecasts, gross booking value rose 21% to $27.7 billion, and the company raised its full-year growth outlook to the high teens.
body:
• Airbnb reported third-quarter revenue of $4.87 billion, up 19% from $4.10 billion a year earlier, and diluted earnings per share of $3.16, up from $2.21, according to its shareholder letter filed with the SEC.
  • Both lines beat expectations: analysts had expected revenue of $4.75 billion and earnings per share of $2.85 on FactSet estimates cited in coverage of the results.
  • Gross booking value rose 21% to $27.7 billion and nights and seats booked rose 16% to 155.0 million, the company reported.
  • Airbnb raised its full-year 2026 outlook to revenue growth in the high teens and an adjusted EBITDA margin of about 36%, guided fourth-quarter revenue to $3.22 billion to $3.28 billion, and authorized up to $12 billion in additional share repurchases.

A beat on both lines

Airbnb beat Wall Street expectations for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, reporting results after the close on Thursday, November 5. Revenue rose about 19% to $4.87 billion, above the $4.75 billion analysts expected, while diluted earnings per share of $3.16 topped the $2.85 consensus and rose from $2.21 a year earlier, Reuters reported. Net income was $1.89 billion, a 39% margin, up from $1.37 billion a year earlier, according to the company's shareholder letter.

Shares rose about 10% in extended trading after the results, Reuters reported, as investors rewarded the beat and the raised outlook.

Bookings did the work

The growth came from booking volume, not just pricing. Gross booking value rose 21% to $27.7 billion, and nights and seats booked — a measure that covers both home stays and the company's newer services bookings — rose 16% to 155.0 million, according to the shareholder letter. The average daily rate rose 4% to $179.

Management said the expansion of its Reserve Now, Pay Later option contributed about three percentage points of the 16% growth in nights and seats booked, Zacks reported from the earnings call. By region, quarterly bookings in North America grew by a low-double-digit rate year over year and grew in the mid-teens in Europe, the Middle East and Africa, Reuters reported. Chief Executive Brian Chesky attributed the acceleration to platform improvements, pricing initiatives and organizational changes, according to Zacks.

Profit and cash

Adjusted EBITDA was $2.5 billion, a 52% margin, supported by revenue growth, cost discipline and AI-related efficiencies, Zacks reported. Airbnb generated $1.4 billion of free cash flow in the quarter, a 29% margin, and $4.9 billion over the trailing twelve months, a 35% margin, according to the shareholder letter. The company held $12.6 billion in cash, short-term investments and restricted cash at September 30.

Efficiency showed up in service costs as well: customer support cost per booking fell more than 17% year over year, as about 40% of issues were resolved without a human agent, up from one-third in the second quarter, Reuters reported.

Outlook and the $12 billion buyback

Airbnb raised its full-year 2026 revenue growth outlook to the high teens, from at least mid-teens previously, and lifted its adjusted EBITDA margin forecast to about 36% from at least 35.5%, according to the shareholder letter and Zacks. For the fourth quarter, the company expects revenue of $3.22 billion to $3.28 billion, growth of 16% to 18% year over year, with gross booking value growth in the mid-teens.

The board authorized up to an additional $12 billion of share repurchases, on top of $2.7 billion remaining under the existing program after $700 million of buybacks in the third quarter, the company reported. Management said underlying global travel demand remains healthy, while flagging developments in Europe and the Middle East as an area it is monitoring closely — the same region where rivals have cited pressure from higher airfares and unrest, according to Reuters.

What to watch next

Two checks matter from here: whether fourth-quarter revenue lands inside the $3.22 billion to $3.28 billion guide during the holiday season, and whether booking growth holds once the Reserve Now, Pay Later lift annualizes. For diaspora readers, the read-across is simple: international leisure demand stayed firm through the autumn.
